gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Fluance's own store sells a third preamp-equipped deck, the RT80 Classic, for $249.99. That is the same price as the AT-LP70X, and its spec table gives the same switchable PHONO/LINE preamp with full bypass, 140 mV line output and 67 dB A-weighted S/N as the $299.99 RT81. Fluance's compare table lists only two differences from the RT81: an AT91 cartridge instead of the AT95E, and a felt mat instead of a rubber one.
standout_why: I compared against valveandvinyl.com/turntables/crosley-alternatives (2026-11-07), platterandplinth.com/turntables/best-with-preamp (updated 2026-08-19) and fewbetter.com/best-turntable-with-built-in-phono-preamp. Both valveandvinyl and platterandplinth already price the AT-LP70X ($249), RT81 ($299.99), AT-LP120XUSB ($349) and AT-LP60X/60XBT, and platterandplinth prices the PS-LX3BT at $398. Neither names the Fluance RT80, the RT81+ price, or a line-output level for any deck. The fewbetter page fetched with no models at all. I did not open the other 10 result pages, so the claim that no result mentions the RT80 rests on these three.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's pair (LP70X for automatic play, RT81 for manual) and sharpens the low end. At $249–250 the choice is automatic play (LP70X) against a manual deck with Fluance's published 67 dB A-weighted S/N and full preamp bypass (RT80). For the RT81 against the RT81+, Fluance's specs list the same phono stage, S/N and wow & flutter. The extra $50 buys the VM95E cartridge (4.0 mV), an acrylic mat, adjustable feet and a damped platter, not a better preamp. For the Sony PS-LX3BT, the prices I could open were higher than ChatGPT's card, and both Sony replacement styli Turntable Lab lists are out of stock.

Its weak point is the cartridge: the spec table lists an AT91 (0.6 mil conical, 3.5 mV), but the Features text names the AT95E, so the page contradicts itself. It is manual with defeatable auto-stop, not fully automatic. That is where it loses to the LP70X for a beginner.
